decisions.label: Overlap I/O
decisions.brief: Off: the experts are computed on the device, beside its cache.
decisions.reason: overlap hides the CPU's expert compute behind the streamer's reads, and with the device expert cache armed the experts are computed on CUDA0, so there is nothing on the CPU for it to hide

decisions.label: Device expert cache
decisions.brief: A 16.4 GiB cache of the most used experts on CUDA0, in place of whole layers' experts.
decisions.reason: the experts used most live on the processor that computes them fastest, as the RAM cache holds what flash would read: CUDA0 computes this model's experts at 428 GiB/s against the host's 40, both measured on this model's own expert block; a cache of 16809 MiB (16795 the capacity fitter gave 36 of 40 layers' experts, 13 it left free under one more whole layer) serves 90% of a token's routed bytes (the fraction of the expert set it holds); a miss is uploaded from the host

decisions.label: Batch width
decisions.brief: A prompt runs in one pass: that takes only 1.0 GiB.
decisions.reason: a graph as wide as the context reserves 1024 MiB of compute buffers, inside 10% of the 105831 MiB this process may hold: a prompt is computed in one pass

decisions.label: Layer placement
decisions.brief: 41 layers on a device; 40 of 40 layers keep their experts on the CPU.
decisions.reason: the capacity fitter found a placement that is projected to fit; 40 of 40 MoE layers keep their experts on the host, host-resident 1024 MiB, on devices 6078 MiB, context 16384 (fitter's host breakdown: model 2444, context 0, compute 1024 MiB; file 21098, experts 18662)

decisions.label: Context
decisions.brief: 16384 tokens of context, as given: not weighed against the cache.
decisions.reason: the value this run was given, not a choice: the capacity fitter only picks a context when it is handed a zero and this planner always pins it, so nothing has weighed this number against what the memory it reserves would buy as expert cache

decisions.label: Streaming mode
decisions.brief: The whole model (19.7 GiB) fits in the 82.7 GiB usable.
decisions.reason: on the host 20210 MiB (dense 1548) against 84665 MiB usable, which is the 105831 MiB this process may hold (as reported available, unmeasured) less a 21166 MiB margin (the process is killed)

decisions.label: Experts in a device's host memory
decisions.brief: The experts copied into CUDA0's own host memory, for the cache's misses.
decisions.reason: a miss reaches CUDA0 at 11.9 GiB/s from the file's mapping and at 22.6 from the backend's own host memory; the copy takes 18662 MiB, inside the 84665 MiB the host may hold with the 20210 MiB it already does

decisions.label: Expert streaming
decisions.brief: Not streamed: the whole model fits in memory.
decisions.reason: the host residual fits: llama.cpp's placement is the whole plan

decisions.label: Compute threads
decisions.brief: 16 threads: the fastest count measured on this model's format.
decisions.reason: swept over the thread counts this machine has, on a matmul in this model's own quantized format, which is the material that matters: a sweep in F32 can pick a count the quantized kernels are much slower at

decisions.label: Thread counts to measure
decisions.brief: The first answer measures 8 threads against 16.
decisions.reason: the thread count changes no output and which one decodes fastest is this machine's answer, not a rule's: once the cache has settled the first real request alternates decode windows between 16 and 8 (where a slower class of core starts, every core, or half of them where all are alike), and switches only to a count 10% faster in the median of its rounds; the next load starts from the verdict
